title: Sale / share determination (CCPA)
tag: Decide whether a data flow is a 'sale' or a 'share' that triggers opt-out, contracts, and minor-consent rules.
q: Is this data flow a 'sale' in California's eyes?

q-business.q: Does your organization qualify as a 'business' under CCPA § 1798.140(d)?
q-business.help: A 'business' is a for-profit California-doing-business entity that determines the purposes and means of processing and meets ≥1 threshold: (A) annual gross revenue over the statutory $25M base as CPI-adjusted under §1798.185(a)(5) — the operative figure is $26,625,000 effective January 1, 2025, and it adjusts every odd-numbered year (next adjustment due January 2027; verify the current figure); (B) annually buys/sells/shares personal information (PI) of ≥100,000 consumers or households; (C) ≥50% revenue from selling/sharing PI. Thresholds (B) and (C) are not monetary and are not CPI-adjusted.

opts.label: Yes — meets a threshold and does business in CA
Affiliate of a covered business with shared branding and PI sharing
opts.desc: §1798.140(d)(2) covers controlled affiliates that share common branding and PI

o-not-business.title: Not a 'business' under CCPA — § 1798.120 doesn't apply
o-not-business.summary: Without §1798.140(d) coverage, the sale/share opt-out and § 1798.135 link/signal duties don't attach. But monitor the thresholds — they are measured annually.
actions: Monitor revenue and consumer/household counts quarterly. The revenue threshold looks at the preceding calendar year, so coverage starts with the new calendar year once revenue passes the CPI-adjusted figure. The 100,000-consumer/household and 50%-revenue thresholds have no January-1 trigger — assume coverage starts as soon as the annual measure is met, unless regulatory guidance says otherwise

Even if you're not a 'business', obligations may still reach you downstream — via individual employees and the service-provider contracts you sign; confirm those contracts don't accidentally make you a 'business'

q-relationship.q: What is the recipient's relationship to your business?
q-relationship.help: The recipient's status drives whether a flow is a sale/share or an internal use. § 1798.140 distinguishes service providers (ag), contractors (j), and third parties (ai). Service providers and contractors operate under written contracts with strict use limitations.

opts.label: Service provider — processes on behalf of business, written contract prohibits sale/share
Contractor — written contract with same restrictions as service provider
Third party — independent recipient (not a service provider, not a contractor)

q-sp-contract.q: Does the written contract contain ALL the required service-provider/contractor restrictions?
q-sp-contract.help: §1798.140(ag)(1): the contract must prohibit (A) selling/sharing the PI, (B) retaining/using/disclosing outside the contracted business purpose, (C) retaining/using outside the direct business relationship, (D) combining PI from this business with PI from another source (limited business-purpose exceptions).

opts.label: Yes — all four prohibitions are in writing
No — contract is silent or incomplete on one or more

o-not-sale-not-share.title: Not a sale and not a share — service provider / contractor exception applies
o-not-sale-not-share.summary: Disclosure of PI to a properly contracted service provider (SP)/contractor for a business purpose is not a 'sale' under §1798.140(ad) and not a 'share' under §1798.140(ah). Make sure the contract is robust, the limitations are observed in practice, and the SP/contractor is genuinely operating on your behalf — not for its own ends.
actions: Confirm the SP/contractor agreement contains all four §1798.140(ag)(1)/(j)(1) prohibitions

Consider negotiating contract rights to monitor/audit SP/contractor compliance — § 1798.140(ag)(1) permits the contract, subject to agreement with the service provider, to allow monitoring including audits at least once every 12 months (this is permissive contract language, not a statutory duty)
Confirm sub-processors are flowed-through contractually (§1798.140(ag)(2)/(j)(2))
You do not need a 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link if your only disclosures are to properly contracted service providers/contractors and there are no third-party flows
Maintain mapping of which vendors are SP/contractor vs third party

o-defective-sp.title: Treat as a third-party disclosure — sale/share analysis required
o-defective-sp.summary: Without a §1798.140(ag)/(j)-compliant written contract, the recipient is by default a 'third party' under §1798.140(ai), and the disclosure has to be evaluated as a sale or share.
actions: Immediately upgrade the contract with the four required prohibitions, or treat the flow as a sale/share and implement the full opt-out obligations
Inventory all vendors and confirm contract terms
Update notice at collection and privacy policy to disclose third-party flows if you keep treating them as such

q-third-purpose.q: What's the purpose of disclosing to this third party?
q-third-purpose.help: §1798.140(ad)(1) — 'sale' requires monetary OR other valuable consideration. §1798.140(ah)(1) — 'share' requires use for cross-context behavioral advertising (CCBA), regardless of consideration. These categories overlap: a disclosure can be both.

opts.label: For non-monetary 'valuable consideration' (e.g. enhanced services in exchange)
For cross-context behavioral advertising (CCBA) — targeting ads across distinct businesses
The consumer directed us to disclose to / interact with the third party
Passing along an opt-out — sharing an identifier so the third party knows the consumer has opted out
Transfer as part of M&A / bankruptcy
None of the above — internal-only use

o-sale.title: This is a 'sale' under § 1798.140(ad)
o-sale.summary: You must offer consumers the right to opt out of sale (§ 1798.120(a)) and operationalize it. Under the CPPA regulations, honoring opt-out preference signals (e.g. the Global Privacy Control (GPC)) is mandatory for every business that sells or shares PI (11 CCR § 7025(b)); the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link (§ 1798.135(a)) is additionally required unless you process the signal in a frictionless manner (11 CCR § 7025(f)–(g)).
actions: Honor opt-out preference signals (e.g. GPC) — this is mandatory under 11 CCR § 7025(b) for any business that sells or shares PI; it is not an alternative you can decline by posting a link

Also add a clear and conspicuous 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link on your homepage (§ 1798.135(a)) — the link may be omitted only if you process opt-out preference signals in a 'frictionless manner' under 11 CCR § 7025(f)–(g); a single combined link with 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' is permitted
Update privacy notice and notice at collection to disclose the sale and explain the opt-out right
If the consumer is known to be under 16: do not sell without affirmative opt-in (from the consumer if 13–15; from the parent if under 13) — § 1798.120(c)
Wait at least 12 months before reauthorization requests (§ 1798.135(c)(4))

Notify third parties to whom you sold/shared the PI of opt-out requests and direct them to comply (11 CCR § 7026(f)(2)); verifying downstream compliance is recommended practice — the statute itself imposes no audit duty

Conduct and document a CCPA risk assessment — the CPPA's 2025 risk-assessment regulations treat selling/sharing PI as a significant-risk activity (11 CCR § 7150 et seq.); verify the final section numbers and phased submission/retention deadlines against the current regulation text

o-share.title: This is a 'share' under § 1798.140(ah) — CCBA-specific
o-share.summary: Cross-context behavioral advertising is 'sharing' even with no money changing hands. The opt-out obligations are the same as for a sale: honoring opt-out preference signals is mandatory, and the homepage link is required unless you process the signal in a frictionless manner.
actions: Honor opt-out preference signals (e.g. the Global Privacy Control (GPC)) — mandatory under 11 CCR § 7025(b) for any business sharing PI for CCBA; the 'Do Not Sell or Share' homepage link is additionally required unless you process the signal in a frictionless manner per 11 CCR § 7025(f)–(g)

Confirm whether any vendor classified as 'service provider' is actually performing CCBA — § 1798.140(e)(6) carves cross-context behavioral advertising out of the service-provider business purposes, so a vendor doing CCBA for you is by definition a third party
Minor consent (under 16) rule applies — § 1798.120(c)
12-month reauthorization wait — § 1798.135(c)(4)
Update notice at collection: must disclose categories of PI shared and the consumer's right to opt out

Conduct and document a CCPA risk assessment — the CPPA's 2025 risk-assessment regulations treat selling/sharing PI as a significant-risk activity (11 CCR § 7150 et seq.); verify the final section numbers and phased submission/retention deadlines against the current regulation text

o-consumer-directed.title: Not a sale or share — consumer-directed disclosure exception
o-consumer-directed.summary: § 1798.140(ad)(2)(A) and (ah)(2)(A): a business does not sell or share when a consumer uses or directs the business to intentionally disclose PI or interact with one or more third parties.
actions: Confirm the consumer's direction is intentional and documented (UI flow, click-through, etc.)
Do not extend the exception to incidental disclosures made alongside the consumer's directed action — only the directed disclosure is covered
Hovering, muting, pausing, or closing content is not 'intentional interaction' (§ 1798.140(s))
Avoid dark patterns — consent obtained through a dark pattern is invalid (§ 1798.140(h))

o-optout-signal.title: Not a sale or share — opt-out signal/identifier carve-out
o-optout-signal.summary: § 1798.140(ad)(2)(B) and (ah)(2)(B): disclosing or sharing an identifier solely to alert downstream parties that the consumer has opted out is not a sale or share. This is the foundation of opt-out propagation.
actions: Use this carve-out only for opt-out propagation, not for any other purpose
Document the identifier-purpose narrowly in your vendor contracts

o-mna.title: Not a sale or share — M&A / asset transfer carve-out, but with conditions
o-mna.summary: § 1798.140(ad)(2)(C) and (ah)(2)(C): transfer of PI as an asset in a merger, acquisition, bankruptcy, or other transaction in which the third party assumes control of the business is not a sale or share, provided the PI is used or shared consistently with the CCPA. If the buyer materially changes use, it must give prior notice and opportunity to exercise rights.
actions: Include a representation in transaction docs that the buyer will honor existing privacy promises
If buyer plans to change use materially, build prior-notice obligation into the deal
Do not use this carve-out for ordinary marketing transfers — it applies only to M&A-type transactions

As a practical/diligence matter, have the buyer honor consumers' pre-transfer opt-out directions: the carve-out holds only if the transferred PI is used or shared consistently with the CCPA (§ 1798.140(ad)(2)(C)/(ah)(2)(C)), and materially inconsistent use requires prior notice — there is no separate statutory 'carry-over' rule

o-affiliate.title: Affiliate disclosures — (d)(2) makes the affiliate a covered 'business'; sale/share treatment of inter-affiliate flows is unsettled
o-affiliate.summary: § 1798.140(d)(2) makes a controlled affiliate that shares common branding with a covered business, and with whom the business shares consumers' PI, itself a covered 'business.' It does not clearly merge the affiliates into one business for CCPA purposes: an affiliate that is not the consumer-facing business and is not contracted as an SP/contractor is arguably a 'third party' under § 1798.140(ai), so a transfer for consideration or for CCBA could still be a sale/share.
actions: Confirm all three (d)(2) elements: control (e.g. >50% voting ownership or controlling influence), common branding (shared name/servicemark/trademark recognizable to consumers), and that the business shares consumers' PI with the affiliate

Safest course: put a § 1798.140(ag)/(j)-compliant SP/contractor contract between the affiliates, or run the third-party sale/share analysis on the inter-affiliate flow rather than assuming it is intra-business
If common branding (or any other (d)(2) element) is missing, treat the affiliate as a third party and run the third-party flow analysis

o-internal.title: Not a sale or share — internal use only
o-internal.summary: Internal use of PI within a single business doesn't implicate § 1798.120. Confirm the use is consistent with the notice at collection and § 1798.100(c) data minimization / purpose limitation.
actions: Confirm purpose compatibility with notice at collection
Watch for 'further processing' for new purposes — may need new disclosure or consent under § 1798.100(c)
